hotspot_events.title: NVIDIA FY2027 Q3 Earnings Beat Expectations, Q4 Guidance $130 billion
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Revenue $115.8 billion, +103% YoY; data center $107.6 billion, +110% YoY; Q4 guidance $130 billion; Rubin NVL72 has started shipping; renewed AI compute demand will further intensify competition for generic material capacity
hotspot_events.summary: NVIDIA FY2027 Q3 revenue $115.8 billion (YoY +103%, about 7.2% above guidance), data center revenue $107.6 billion (YoY +110%, representing roughly 93% of total revenue), adjusted EPS $2.68 (consensus $2.47), GAAP gross margin 74.8%; Q4 guidance revenue $130 billion (±3%), gross margin guidance down to 71%–72%, Q4 covers 14 weeks and continues to assume zero computing revenue from Chinese data centers; the Vera Rubin NVL72 system has begun shipping; interim CEO Colette Kress raised FY2028 revenue growth outlook from 70% to 75%; new chairman Harvey Jones said the board has no intention of reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO; stock closed at $155.46 (‑0.44%, down about 24% since November), briefly rose in after‑hours to $161.70 (+4.0%).

hotspot_events.title: U.S. BIS 11‑16 New Chip Export Controls Effective 11‑19
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Added final-use controls for data centers to close remote compute leasing loophole via third‑country providers; Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Brazil now require additional licenses; delivery pace of Southeast Asian data‑center hubs faces slowdown
hotspot_events.summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce BIS issued a temporary final rule on 11‑16 titled “Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors,” adding §744.24 data‑center final‑use controls: when exporting advanced chips and servers to any data center worldwide, if the exporter knows that the data center provides compute access exceeding 12 million total processing performance (TPP) to enterprises headquartered in China, Macau, or the D:5 country group, a license must be obtained, with a 90‑day transition period for existing data centers providing such compute; exports of advanced AI items to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil now require additional licenses (case‑by‑case review); the rule also formally repeals the Biden‑era “AI Diffusion Rule” and removes model‑weight controls; NVIDIA’s Q4 guidance continues to assume zero computing revenue from Chinese data centers, consistent with this rule.

industry_updates.title: Vertiv Launches 800VDC Three-Tier Power Expansion
industry_updates.detail: Vertiv launched its 800VDC combined expansion on Nov 17: adding PowerDirect 9000 (AI computing pod-level) and PowerNexus MV SST (5MW solid-state transformer, medium-voltage AC primary conversion to 800VDC), covering three-tier deployment of rack/pod/data hall; showcased at SC26 on Nov 17–22, with pilot projects and customer collaborative development underway.

industry_updates.title: Shenling Acquires 260 Mu of Land to Build Liquid-Cooled Computing Infrastructure Intelligent Manufacturing Base
industry_updates.detail: Shenling acquired over 260 mu of industrial land in Chencun, Shunde on Nov 16 to build a liquid-cooled computing infrastructure intelligent manufacturing base (integrating R&D final assembly, upstream supporting, R&D verification, cross-border export, and industrial incubation); the liquid-cooling new-quality intelligent manufacturing base in Chencun with a total investment of 8 billion RMB broke ground this March; CAICT estimates the domestic liquid-cooling market at 70–105 billion RMB in 2026, with an annual growth rate exceeding 70%.

industry_updates.title: Trane Unveils Presence at Data Centre World Paris Starting Today
industry_updates.detail: Trane is showcasing the LiquidStack 1MW CDU and GigaModular hybrid cooling solutions at Data Centre World Paris on Nov 18–19.

industry_updates.title: Daikin D60-W 60MW AI Factory Liquid-Cooling Reference Architecture
industry_updates.detail: Daikin D60-W 60MW AI factory liquid-cooling reference architecture (official website Nov 11): based on NVIDIA DSX AI Factory platform and Vera Rubin NVL72, six units, 92% liquid-cooled / 8% air-cooled, classified as a reference design, un-shipped, with no customer deployments.

industry_updates.title: JCI Sues LG for Magnetic-Bearing Centrifugal Chiller Patent Infringement
industry_updates.detail: JCI filed a patent infringement lawsuit against LG Electronics in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas on Nov 09, claiming that the heat exchanger technology used in its newly launched York YDAM air-cooled magnetic-bearing centrifugal chiller (up to 3.5MW) is protected by U.S. Patent No. 9,869,487, and that LG's recently released air-cooled magnetic-bearing centrifugal chillers and supply agreements constitute infringement; the case is in the litigation stage and the court has not yet ruled.

industry_updates.title: EU CBAM: Court Confirms Legality, Deduction Implementing Regulation Issued
industry_updates.detail: The Court of Justice of the European Union dismissed Poland's lawsuit seeking to annul CBAM on Nov 12, confirming the mechanism's legality; downstream scope expansion trilogue negotiations are scheduled for Nov 30 (scheduled to take effect Jan 01, 2028); the European Commission issued Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/2498 on Nov 16, clarifying carbon price deduction rules for third countries (international carbon credit deduction cap at 10%); the suspension of gallium/germanium/antimony export bans to the US is still set to expire on Nov 27, with no extension announcements as of Nov 17.

siphon_effects.detail: NVIDIA FY2027 Q3 revenue reached $115.8 billion (+103% YoY), data center revenue $107.6 billion (+110% YoY), Q4 guidance $130 billion, Rubin NVL72 shipments beginning; encroachment of AI servers on general-purpose material capacities such as DRAM/HBM, MLCC, high multi-layer PCBs, and high-speed copper-clad laminates (CCL) will further intensify.

October general-purpose DDR4 8Gb average contract price reached $27.5 (+5.77% MoM, hitting another historical high); TrendForce expects Q4 DRAM contract prices up 10%–15%, NAND up 15%–20%; SK Hynix stated it has signed 5-year long-term contracts with 14 core customers, locking in over 50% of total capacity for 2027–2028, with DRAM and HBM capacity nearly sold out through 2029, and customer intended purchase volume reaching twice the existing supply; Samsung's 2027 HBM supply negotiations have concluded and capacity is fully sold out.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics lead times have extended to 52 weeks, with high-capacitance product price hikes for AI servers reaching 50%–80% (industry collation basis), and negotiating a further quarter-on-quarter increase of over 25%; Murata's high-end production line capacity utilization exceeds 90%, with an additional 80 billion yen invested in high-end MLCCs; TrendForce judges that high-end shortages will extend to the first half of 2027, with Q1–Q2 2027 being the most severe; the supply chain initiated 2027 Q1 price negotiations in November 2026.

Panasonic's Hukou plant in Taiwan remains shut down (as of Nov 10) following a fire (Nov 04); the plant is a core base for MEGTRON M6/M7/M8, accounting for approximately 20% of the global capacity for this series, and TrendForce assesses that about 4% of global high-end CCL supply faces disruption risks; Shengyi Technology stated on Nov 09 that copper-clad laminate capacity is tight, with further price adjustments expected in November; this round of CCL price increases has run for 4–5 quarters, with a conservative expectation of monthly price-hike momentum continuing until June 2027.

Combined 2026 capex guidance for Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta totals $720–740 billion (Alphabet alone at $195–205 billion); Oracle fiscal 2027 capex guidance is $90–95 billion; CoreWeave's full-year capex guidance was raised to $37–39 billion (approx. 3x revenue), with order backlog at $132.5 billion.

Average lead time for large U.S. power transformers is about 128 weeks, generator step-up transformers about 144 weeks, switchgear about 44 weeks, and high-voltage circuit breakers reached 125 weeks in the second half of 2025; delivery cycles for Chinese manufacturers are only 10–12 months, and urgent orders can be compressed to 6 months; China's transformer exports in 2025 reached 64.6 billion RMB (+36%), with an average unit price of 205,000 RMB.
siphon_effects.source: Wood Mackenzie via Plant to Pipeline, 2026-11-05

cross_industry.detail: Samsung's talks to acquire Modine (Modexus Solutions) show no new progress within the window, with the latest status remaining Bloomberg's Nov 13 scoop—neither side has confirmed, no final decision has been made, talks may break down, and other bidders may emerge; Modine is scheduled to hold its Analyst and Investor Day today, Nov 18 at 10:00 AM ET, where it will update its multi-year growth strategy and new financial targets; Korean media estimates the acquisition price including premium at $7.5–8.0 billion (unconfirmed, media estimate only).

From January to July 2026, domestic Chinese IGBT suppliers collectively accounted for 62% of domestic installations; 8-inch production lines were crowded out by AI server power supply demand, extending lead times from 8–12 weeks to over 30 weeks, with some part numbers delayed up to 52 weeks; MOSFET prices have risen over 10% since July, with high-end part numbers up over 20%; Jiejie Microelectronics announced on Nov 17 plans to invest 1.5 billion RMB to build an automotive-grade high-power semiconductor device chip production line (1200V/2300V/3300V automotive MOSFETs and power modules), targeting NEV electronic control, PV inverters, charging piles, energy storage, computing power power supplies, and industrial variable-frequency drives (VFDs).

ST's fourth round of price adjustments effective Jan 01, 2027: the fourth round within 2026, raising prices for selected products (automotive, MCUs, power devices), following three previous rounds of price adjustments; TI has accumulatively adjusted prices 5 times within 2026, and NXP and onsemi have also raised prices; SiC MOSFET and module lead times are 48–52 weeks, with 6-inch substrate plant capacity utilization generally exceeding 90%.

Huawei Digital Power customer letter in October (reported Nov 04): residential/commercial/industrial/utility-scale PV inverters and energy storage up 5%–15%, grid-forming utility-scale energy storage PCS up 5%–10%, with no unified effective date and negotiated customer-by-customer, attributed to copper, PCB, and electronic component costs; Sungrow up 5%–15% starting Sep 20, Kehua full-line up 5%–15% starting Nov 01, KSTAR up 10%–20%.

U.S. October retail sales reached $748.2 billion, +0.2% MoM (in line with expectations, September unrevised at +0.8%), +6.8% YoY, but the ±0.4 percentage point margin of error includes zero, making actual growth statistically unconfirmed, and the data is not adjusted for inflation (October CPI +0.4% MoM), resulting in negative actual sales after adjusting for inflation; the FOMC Oct 27–28 meeting minutes will be released at 03:00 Beijing time on Nov 19.
